title: Three witnesses will see the plates, but humility comes first
setting: Martin Harris traveled to Harmony, Pennsylvania, in March 1829. There is no record that he and Joseph Smith had met since the manuscript was lost in 1828. Around Palmyra, opposition to the plates was growing, and Harris’s wife Lucy led much of it. She filed a complaint before a magistrate in Lyons, New York, alleging fraud. Harris came wanting a further witness that Joseph truly had the plates, and this revelation answered his request.
summary: The revelation answers Martin Harris’s wish for a witness that Joseph had the plates. It says Joseph covenanted to show the plates only to those the Lord names. His first gift is to translate, and he should claim no other until that is finished. If people will not believe God’s words, they would not believe even if Joseph showed them everything. It promises three witnesses who will be shown the plates by God’s power. Joseph is told to repent and to yield to the persuasions of men no more. Harris can be a witness if he humbles himself in mighty prayer and faith; then he may only say he has seen them. If Harris does not humble himself, Joseph is to translate a few more pages and then stop until commanded again.

contextNote.title: Why Martin Harris had to wait
contextNote.text: Martin Harris wanted proof that the plates were real. Verse 24 names what stood in his way: he “exalts himself and does not humble himself sufficiently” before God. The condition it sets is humility in “mighty prayer and faith,” not a better argument. Verse 7 explains why a display alone would not work. People who reject God’s words would not believe even if Joseph showed them everything. Verse 28 states the reverse: without humility, Harris will have “no such views” at all. In this revelation, a witness is a view granted to the humble, not evidence handed to a doubter.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 3–5 teaches that through the Holy Ghost we can gain a witness of the Book of Mormon. Compare verses 16 and 24: what does each say a person must do before receiving a witness?

newPlaces.name: Lyons, New York
newPlaces.why: Setting: Lucy Harris filed a complaint before a magistrate there in 1829, and Martin Harris testified at the hearing (JSP historical introduction).

reviewNote: Read all 35 verses. Official heading gives Harmony, March 1829, at Martin Harris’s request. JSP historical introduction read for the growing Palmyra opposition, Lucy Harris’s complaint at Lyons, and Harris’s wish for a greater witness. Lyons added as a new place for the setting; drop it if the map should show only text-named places. Lucy Harris is not named in the text and was not added as a person. Fact-check 2026-10-12: summary now includes the command for Joseph to repent (v. 21) and states that the stop-translating instruction (v. 30) is conditional on Harris not humbling himself.
